classes.objetivo: Detectar pistas de que un narrador no es fiable, leer entre líneas y deducir qué pasó realmente con must have, can't have y might have.

vocabulario.es: interesado, que favorece al propio narrador

ensenanza.en: An unreliable narrator is not always a liar; he may simply misjudge events, forget details or conceal what he is ashamed of.
ensenanza.es: Un narrador poco fiable no siempre es un mentiroso; puede simplemente juzgar mal los hechos, olvidar detalles u ocultar aquello de lo que se avergüenza.
ensenanza.nota: Poco fiable no significa mentiroso: el narrador puede equivocarse o callar sin mala intención.

ensenanza.en: A single clue, such as a date or a muddy boot, can cast doubt on the narrator's version of events.
ensenanza.es: Una sola pista, como una fecha o una bota embarrada, puede poner en duda la versión de los hechos del narrador.
ensenanza.nota: Cast doubt on + algo: una pista sembrada en el texto debilita lo que se cuenta.

ensenanza.en: When a story feels suspicious, read between the lines: what a narrator leaves out matters as much as what he says.
ensenanza.es: Cuando una historia resulta sospechosa, lee entre líneas: lo que el narrador omite importa tanto como lo que dice.
ensenanza.nota: Suspicious describe lo que hace dudar; leer entre líneas es fijarse en lo no dicho.

ensenanza.en: He will claim he stayed in, but mud on his boots means he must have been out after dark.
ensenanza.es: Afirmará que se quedó en casa, pero el barro de sus botas indica que tuvo que salir después de anochecer.
ensenanza.nota: Must have + participio: deducción casi segura sobre el pasado, apoyada en una pista.

ensenanza.en: A self-serving narrator may exaggerate his courage and gloss over his mistakes, so the storm might have been milder.
ensenanza.es: Un narrador interesado puede exagerar su valentía y quitar importancia a sus errores, así que la tormenta pudo haber sido más suave.
ensenanza.nota: Might have + participio: posibilidad sin certeza. Gloss over: tratar un fallo como si no importara.

ensenanza.en: If two witnesses contradict each other, one of them can't have remembered events accurately, so the reader must weigh both.
ensenanza.es: Si dos testigos se contradicen, uno de ellos no puede haber recordado los hechos con exactitud, así que el lector debe sopesar ambos.
ensenanza.nota: Can't have + participio: casi seguro que no ocurrió. Para deducir no se usa mustn't have.

explicacion.titulo: Desconfiar del narrador y deducir el pasado
explicacion.texto: Un narrador poco fiable cuenta la historia de un modo que no puedes aceptar sin más: se equivoca, exagera, oculta algo o solo ve una parte. Las pistas son detalles que chocan con su versión: un objeto, una fecha, la reacción de otro personaje. Para reconstruir lo ocurrido usa modal + have + participio: must have (casi seguro que pasó), can't have (casi seguro que no pasó) y might o could have (posible). En español dirías «debió de» o «no pudo»; en inglés la negación de la deducción es can't, nunca mustn't.

formula.texto: The narrator says he stayed in,
but mud on his boots
means he must have been out.
formula.nota: casi seguro que ocurrió: must have + participio

formula.texto: He can't have forgotten; he might have lied.
formula.nota: casi seguro que no / posible: can't have, might have

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: He mustn't have been at home: a neighbour saw him at the station.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: He can't have been at home: a neighbour saw him at the station.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Para deducir que algo casi seguro no ocurrió se usa can't have; mustn't expresa prohibición, no deducción.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: She might have exaggerating the story to look good.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: She might have exaggerated the story to look good.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Después de might have va siempre el participio (exaggerated), no la forma en -ing.

situacion.contexto: Ana y Leo comentan una novela de misterio cuyo narrador asegura que pasó la noche en casa.

dialogo.texto: The narrator claims he stayed in all night, but the mud on his boots is a clue.
dialogo.traduccion: El narrador afirma que se quedó en casa toda la noche, pero el barro de sus botas es una pista.

dialogo.texto: I agree. He must have been out, and he tries to gloss over it.
dialogo.traduccion: De acuerdo. Tuvo que salir, y trata de quitarle importancia.

dialogo.texto: Maybe he wants to conceal something worse. He might have been at the station.
dialogo.traduccion: Quizá quiere ocultar algo peor. Puede que estuviera en la estación.

dialogo.texto: We have to read between the lines. That clue casts doubt on his whole version of events.
dialogo.traduccion: Hay que leer entre líneas. Esa pista pone en duda toda su versión de los hechos.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué deduce Leo a partir del barro de las botas?

opciones.es: Que el narrador salió de casa aunque lo niega.
Que el narrador caminó por el jardín por la mañana.
Que otro personaje usó las botas del narrador.

item.feedback: Leo dice que el narrador «must have been out» y que intenta quitarle importancia, o sea, que salió aunque lo niegue.

guiada.consigna: Elige la deducción más sólida a partir de la pista del texto.
guiada.texto: «I spent the whole evening at home with a book,» the narrator insists. Yet the next page mentions that the library had closed at eight and that his coat smelled of rain.
opciones: He must have been outside at some point that evening.
He can't have been outside, because he was reading all night.
He can't have been at the library, so the coat must belong to someone else.
guiada.feedback: Un abrigo que huele a lluvia apoya una deducción con must have; la segunda se fía de la versión del narrador y la tercera inventa un dato que el texto no da.
guiada.pista: Busca la opción que se apoya en el olor a lluvia del abrigo.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Así que no puede haber estado dormido.»
guiada.texto: The narrator says he was asleep by ten. The neighbour, however, heard his car at midnight. So he ___ have been asleep.
guiada.feedback: Si alguien oyó su auto a medianoche, dormir es casi imposible: la deducción negativa se hace con can't have.
guiada.pista: Deducción negativa sobre el pasado: no uses mustn't.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Puede que exagerara su valentía para quedar bien.»
guiada.respuesta: He might have exaggerated his courage to look good
guiada.feedback: Might have + participio plantea una posibilidad sobre el pasado; to look good expresa el motivo.
guiada.pista: Sujeto, might have, participio, y al final el motivo con to.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada detalle del relato con lo que sugiere.
pares: He describes every hour of the day except the one after dinner.
Pasa por alto justo lo que podría comprometerle.
Three neighbours call it a small fire; he says it ruined the house.
He says, without being asked, that he has nothing to hide.
Su defensa no pedida resulta sospechosa.
His diary says he was ill, but a friend's letter says he was at the party.
practica.feedback: Cada detalle apunta a un tipo distinto de no fiabilidad: omisión, exageración, defensa excesiva y contradicción.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige qué concluye la hablante sobre Tom.
practica.audio: I wanted to believe Tom. He told the police, three times, that he had never met the victim, and he never once looked at me. But a receipt from her shop was in his coat, dated the day before. A man with nothing to hide does not repeat himself like that.
opciones: The way he repeats himself makes her doubt him.
Saying the same thing so often proves that he is guilty.
She still believes him, despite the receipt and his refusal to look at her.
practica.feedback: La hablante suma las negativas repetidas y el recibo del día anterior y duda de Tom; no afirma que esté probado que es culpable ni que aún le crea.

practica.consigna: Completa: «Una sola fecha puede poner en duda la historia del narrador.»
practica.texto: The narrator gives every detail of the evening except the time he returned. One date in the letter can ___ doubt on his whole version of events.
practica.feedback: Cast doubt on es la colocación habitual para poner algo en duda con un dato concreto.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué dato del texto contradice con más fuerza a Carlos?
evaluacion.texto: Carlos tells the court that he never saw the contract. «I would have remembered it,» he says, folding his arms and looking at the floor. Later, Sara remarks that he was the first person to ask about the deadline, that he phoned the lawyer twice that week, and that his signature was still wet on the last page of the document.
opciones: His signature was still wet on the last page.
He was the first person to ask about the deadline.
He phoned the lawyer twice that week.
evaluacion.feedback: La firma fresca es una prueba material de que firmó el documento que niega haber visto; preguntar por el plazo o llamar dos veces al abogado solo sugiere interés.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige qué sugiere la hablante sobre la narradora de la novela.
evaluacion.audio: In the third chapter, the narrator describes her brother's wedding in loving detail: the flowers, the music, the speeches. She mentions, almost in passing, that she left before the cake was cut, and that her mother did not speak to her for a month afterwards. She never explains why. Readers who accept her warm tone at face value will miss the gap. Because the most important moment of the whole day is the one she skips, we are invited to suspect that her own behaviour was the reason for the silence.
opciones: She may have caused an argument but avoids saying so.
She dislikes her brother and has hidden it from readers.
She was treated unfairly by her mother, as she herself believes.
evaluacion.feedback: La narradora omite justo el momento clave y el enojo de su madre; el lector deduce que ella pudo ser la causa, no que fuera tratada con injusticia.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Los autores pasan por alto la cifra en una sola frase.»
evaluacion.texto: The report praises the scheme at length. The one figure that looks bad appears only in the last paragraph, where the authors ___ over it in a single sentence.
evaluacion.feedback: Gloss over describe tratar un dato incómodo con prisa, para que no llame la atención.

evaluacion.consigna: Escribe dos deducciones sobre el narrador: una con must have, otra con might have.
evaluacion.texto: Un narrador dice que encontró la puerta abierta y llamó a la policía de inmediato, pero el informe dice que llamó tres horas después y que tenía las llaves en la mano. Escribe dos frases: una con must have y otra con might have.
evaluacion.respuesta: He must have entered the house earlier than he says, because he had the keys in his hand. He might have waited to conceal something.
aceptadas: He must have lied about the door, because he still had the keys. He could have concealed the truth for three hours.
evaluacion.feedback: Una buena respuesta apoya must have en una pista (las llaves o la demora) y deja might o could have para una posibilidad.

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué deja entrever la respuesta de Leo al agente?
repaso.texto: When the police officer asked where he had been on Friday, Leo laughed and said, «Honestly, I could tell you every minute, but my memory is a little vague.» Then he described his Friday in great detail, from breakfast to the late film, apart from the hour between nine and ten, which he never mentioned again.
opciones: That he is nervous about one hour and wants to steer attention away.
That he has a poor memory and cannot be blamed for the gaps.
That he finds the question funny and is making fun of the officer.
repaso.feedback: Dice que su memoria es vaga, pero relata todo con detalle salvo una hora: la vaguedad parece una excusa para evitar esa hora, no una burla ni un olvido real.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «No puede haber leído la carta antes de escribir su respuesta.»
repaso.respuesta: She can't have read the letter before she wrote her reply
repaso.feedback: Can't have + participio niega con casi certeza un hecho pasado; before introduce el momento.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Tom afirma que pasó el viernes en el cine.»
repaso.texto: Tom ___ that he spent Friday at the cinema. However, the receipt in his pocket is from a garage.
repaso.feedback: Claim presenta lo que dice el personaje como algo dudoso, justo antes del dato que lo contradice.

classes.objetivo: Usar con precisión el vocabulario de análisis literario (recurring motif, symbol, foreshadowing, imagery, evoke, allude to, resonate) en una reseña crítica.

ensenanza.en: A recurring motif, such as a locked door, becomes a symbol once it stands for something the characters cannot face.
ensenanza.es: Un motivo recurrente, como una puerta cerrada con llave, se convierte en símbolo cuando representa algo que los personajes no pueden afrontar.
ensenanza.nota: El motivo se repite; el símbolo representa una idea. Un mismo elemento puede ser las dos cosas.

ensenanza.en: Foreshadowing prepares the reader for what follows: a cracked mirror in chapter one may warn of the betrayal in chapter ten.
ensenanza.es: El presagio prepara al lector para lo que viene: un espejo roto en el primer capítulo puede avisar de la traición del décimo.
ensenanza.nota: Foreshadowing anticipa sin decirlo abiertamente; se reconoce al releer.

ensenanza.en: The imagery of fog and wet stone can evoke a deep sense of loneliness without the narrator ever naming the feeling.
ensenanza.es: Las imágenes de niebla y piedra mojada pueden evocar una profunda sensación de soledad sin que el narrador nombre nunca el sentimiento.
ensenanza.nota: Imagery son las imágenes sensoriales; evoke indica que despiertan una emoción.

ensenanza.en: A subtle writer will allude to a scandal rather than describe it, leaving the reader to supply the missing details.
ensenanza.es: Un escritor sutil aludirá a un escándalo en lugar de describirlo, y dejará que el lector complete los detalles que faltan.
ensenanza.nota: Allude to + algo: mencionarlo de pasada, sin desarrollarlo.

ensenanza.en: A novelist can convey a central theme without stating it, which is why many endings are open to interpretation.
ensenanza.es: Un novelista puede transmitir un tema central sin enunciarlo, y por eso muchos finales están abiertos a la interpretación.
ensenanza.nota: Open to interpretation: admite más de una lectura razonable.

ensenanza.en: A heavy-handed symbol explains itself too loudly, whereas a good story can resonate with readers long after the last page.
ensenanza.es: Un símbolo pesado se explica a sí mismo con demasiado ruido, mientras que una buena historia puede calar en los lectores mucho después de la última página.
ensenanza.nota: Resonate with + personas. Heavy-handed es una crítica: falta sutileza.

explicacion.titulo: Motivo, símbolo y tema en una reseña crítica
explicacion.texto: Al analizar una obra distingue varios niveles. El motivo (motif) es un elemento que se repite; el símbolo (symbol) representa una idea; el tema (theme) es la idea general que sostiene la obra; el presagio (foreshadowing) anticipa lo que vendrá. Para valorar el efecto usa verbos como evoke, convey o resonate with, y para el estilo, adjetivos como subtle o heavy-handed. Con allude to mencionas algo de pasada, y open to interpretation indica que el final admite varias lecturas.

formula.texto: The recurring motif of water
formula.nota: el motivo: lo que se repite en la obra

formula.texto: is a symbol of change;
it evokes a sense of loss
and will resonate with readers.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The symbol of the novel is that loss changes people.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: The central theme of the novel is that loss changes people.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Una idea general es un tema (theme); un símbolo es una cosa concreta que representa esa idea.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The ending resonates to many readers.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: The ending resonates with many readers.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Resonate se construye con with, nunca con to: resonate with + personas.

situacion.contexto: Mia y Tom comentan una novela que han leído para la clase de literatura.

dialogo.texto: What is the central theme of the novel?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Cuál es el tema central de la novela?

dialogo.texto: I think it is the cost of ambition. The broken clock is a symbol of lost time.
dialogo.traduccion: Creo que es el precio de la ambición. El reloj roto es un símbolo del tiempo perdido.

dialogo.texto: And the recurring motif of water? Is it foreshadowing?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Y el motivo recurrente del agua? ¿Es un presagio?

dialogo.texto: Yes, the storm in chapter two is foreshadowing. The writer is subtle: she only alludes to the flood.
dialogo.traduccion: Sí, la tormenta del capítulo dos es un presagio. La autora es sutil: solo alude a la inundación.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué simboliza el reloj roto?

opciones.es: El tiempo que se ha perdido.

item.feedback: Tom dice que el reloj roto es «a symbol of lost time».

guiada.consigna: ¿Qué término describe el elemento que reaparece en el texto?
guiada.texto: In chapter one, a red umbrella is left by the river. It returns in chapters four and nine, each time just before something goes wrong for the family.
opciones: A recurring motif whose appearances warn of trouble.
A central theme that the narrator states openly.
A piece of imagery that has no link to the plot.
guiada.feedback: Un objeto que vuelve a aparecer y anuncia problemas es un motivo recurrente con función de presagio; no es un tema ni una imagen suelta.
guiada.pista: Piensa en algo que se repite y, además, avisa de lo que viene.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «El faro se convierte en un símbolo de esperanza.»
guiada.texto: The writer never says that the lighthouse means anything. Yet every time it appears, the characters look up, and it becomes a ___ of hope.
guiada.feedback: Una cosa concreta que representa una idea, como la esperanza, es un símbolo.
guiada.pista: Es una cosa concreta que representa una idea abstracta.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «La autora solo alude al escándalo en una frase.»
guiada.respuesta: The writer only alludes to the scandal in one line
guiada.feedback: Allude to + algo: se menciona de pasada, sin describirlo, que es justo lo sutil.
guiada.pista: Tras alludes va to, y después lo que se menciona.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada recurso con lo que hace en el texto.
pares: Reaparece a lo largo de la obra.
Avisa de lo que vendrá sin decirlo.
Despierta una emoción con detalles sensoriales.
practica.feedback: Cada recurso cumple una función distinta: repetir, representar con insistencia, anticipar con sutileza o despertar emociones.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige por qué la hablante lo llama motivo y no símbolo.
practica.audio: The director keeps returning to the same image: a window left open. Nobody comments on it, yet it appears before every departure. I would call it a motif, not a symbol, because it is not yet clear what the window stands for.
opciones: It keeps returning, but what it stands for is not yet clear.
It is tied to departures, so it plainly stands for the characters' fear of leaving.
It repeats before every departure, so it works mainly as foreshadowing.
practica.feedback: Un motivo se repite; para hablar de símbolo haría falta saber qué representa la ventana, y eso todavía no está claro. Que aparezca antes de cada partida no prueba su significado.

practica.consigna: Completa: «Sus imágenes de ceniza y humo evocan una profunda sensación de pérdida.»
practica.texto: The writer never states that the town is losing its people, and she never describes a single goodbye. Yet her imagery of smoke and dust ___ a deep sense of loss on every page.
practica.feedback: Evoke y convey describen el efecto emocional de las imágenes sobre el lector.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa cuatro frases de la reseña con el término literario adecuado.
evaluacion.texto: Reviewers praise The Long Road for being quiet and gentle: the author never explains how the story is built, so readers must work out the pattern for themselves.
frases: The long road is a recurring ___ that returns in every chapter and links the characters' separate journeys.
A cracked mirror in chapter two ___ the betrayal that comes in chapter ten.
The author ___ to the family's money problems in a single line and then moves on.
The writer's ___ of wind and dry stone evokes a place that time has abandoned.
evaluacion.feedback: Lo que se repite pide motif, lo que anticipa pide foreshadows, mencionar de pasada pide alludes to y las imágenes sensoriales piden imagery.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige qué actitud muestra la crítica hacia el faro de la novela.
evaluacion.audio: I wanted to like the new novel. The lighthouse appears on the first page, and on the second, and on the third, each time described as lonely, patient and faithful. By chapter six the writer has practically written in the margin that it is a symbol of hope. A reader deserves a little more trust. If she had mentioned the lighthouse only twice, I think I would have felt its meaning for myself, and the ending might have resonated far more. As it is, I closed the book feeling that I had been told what to think, page after page, and that is not what I read novels for.
opciones: She feels the writer leaves too little for the reader to work out.
She believes the lighthouse would work better if it appeared more often.
She considers the ending weak because the lighthouse is never explained.
evaluacion.feedback: Critica que el símbolo se repita y se explique tanto que no deja trabajo al lector: es una crítica a la falta de sutileza, no a que aparezca poco ni a un final sin resolver.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «El director lo transmite mediante silencios y frases sin terminar.»
evaluacion.texto: The film never tells us that the relationship is failing. The director ___ it through long silences and broken sentences.
evaluacion.feedback: Convey es el verbo natural para lo que un autor transmite al lector sin decirlo abiertamente.

evaluacion.consigna: Escribe dos frases de reseña: a symbol of y resonate with.
evaluacion.texto: Reseña de una novela: un puente roto simboliza la confianza perdida de una familia, y el final conmoverá a cualquiera que se haya despedido de alguien. Escribe dos frases: una con a symbol of y otra con resonate with.
evaluacion.respuesta: The broken bridge is a symbol of the family's lost trust. The final scene will resonate with anyone who has ever said goodbye.
aceptadas: The broken bridge is a symbol of the trust that the family has lost. The ending resonates with many readers who have lost someone.
evaluacion.feedback: Una buena reseña nombra el símbolo con a symbol of y valora su efecto con resonate with.

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué sugiere el texto sobre el paraguas rojo de la película?
repaso.texto: The director never explains the red umbrella that appears in every scene, and when the film ends with it drifting out of frame, the audience is left to decide whether it marks a loss or a release. Some viewers left the cinema annoyed and talking loudly about the price of the ticket; others stayed in their seats for a long time, silent.
opciones: Its meaning is left open, so viewers can read it differently.
It is a motif the director uses to foreshadow the final scene.
It is an obvious symbol that some viewers find too heavy-handed.
repaso.feedback: El director no lo explica y el público duda entre pérdida y liberación: el final está abierto a interpretación.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Sus imágenes pesadas estropean una novela por lo demás sutil.»
repaso.respuesta: Her heavy-handed imagery spoils an otherwise subtle novel
repaso.feedback: Heavy-handed critica la falta de sutileza, y otherwise subtle marca el contraste con el resto de la novela.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «El final está abierto a interpretación.»
repaso.texto: The two readers disagree about the last page. The ending is ___ to interpretation on purpose, and the author refuses to say what she meant.
repaso.feedback: Open to interpretation es la colocación para un final que admite lecturas distintas.

classes.objetivo: Identificar punto de vista, motivación, tema, tono e inferencia en un fragmento de relato, respondiendo con pruebas del texto.

ensenanza.en: The protagonist narrates her own story, so the narrative viewpoint is limited to what she notices, understands and chooses to tell.
ensenanza.es: La protagonista narra su propia historia, así que el punto de vista narrativo se limita a lo que ella observa, entiende y decide contar.
ensenanza.nota: En primera persona solo vemos lo que el narrador ve: por eso su punto de vista es limitado.

ensenanza.en: The plot may show a woman chasing a promotion, but her underlying motivation is a need to prove her father wrong.
ensenanza.es: La trama puede mostrar a una mujer que persigue un ascenso, pero su motivación de fondo es la necesidad de demostrar que su padre se equivocaba.
ensenanza.nota: La trama es lo que ocurre; la motivación de fondo es lo que empuja al personaje, y rara vez se dice.

ensenanza.en: The tone of a passage is the attitude it carries: a detached tone can report a quarrel as if it were a weather forecast.
ensenanza.es: El tono de un pasaje es la actitud que transmite: un tono distante puede contar una discusión como si fuera un pronóstico del tiempo.
ensenanza.nota: Tone se identifica con adjetivos (detached, bitter, tender) y se apoya con pruebas del texto.

ensenanza.en: A wry remark, such as calling a failed dinner a great success, shows amusement and disappointment at the same time.
ensenanza.es: Un comentario irónico, como llamar gran éxito a una cena fallida, muestra diversión y decepción a la vez.
ensenanza.nota: Wry indica humor seco que suele esconder otro sentimiento.

ensenanza.en: To infer a feeling, watch what a character does: she may be reluctant to admit that she still misses him.
ensenanza.es: Para inferir un sentimiento, fíjate en lo que hace un personaje: puede ser reacia a admitir que todavía lo echa de menos.
ensenanza.nota: Infer es deducir lo que el texto no dice con palabras; reluctant to admit + verbo.

ensenanza.en: In hindsight, her bitter comments about the wedding read as grief, and the betrayal she describes is perhaps her own.
ensenanza.es: Visto en retrospectiva, sus comentarios amargos sobre la boda se leen como duelo, y la traición que describe quizá sea la suya.
ensenanza.nota: In hindsight: con lo que sabemos después. Bitter describe un tono resentido.

explicacion.titulo: Leer un relato con cinco preguntas
explicacion.texto: Para comprender un fragmento hazte cinco preguntas. ¿Quién cuenta la historia y qué ve? Es el punto de vista. ¿Qué quiere de verdad el personaje? Es su motivación de fondo, que rara vez se dice. ¿Cómo suena el texto? Es el tono: distante, amargo, irónico. ¿De qué trata en el fondo? Es el tema. ¿Qué no se dice, pero se adivina? Eso se infiere. Responde siempre con una prueba: The tone is bitter, because… / We can infer that…, because…

patron.texto: Pregunta de análisis + respuesta con prueba:

formula.texto: The protagonist tells the story in the first person,
so the narrative viewpoint is limited.
formula.nota: punto de vista: lo que ve y lo que calla

formula.texto: The tone is bitter,
because every memory ends in a complaint.
formula.nota: la prueba: siempre con because o for example

filas.texto: It is told in the first person.
She wants to prove him wrong.
We can infer that she is afraid.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The history of the film follows a man who loses his job.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: The plot of the film follows a man who loses his job.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: History es la historia del pasado; para el argumento de una obra se dice plot.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Is clear that the narrator is reluctant to admit it.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: It is clear that the narrator is reluctant to admit it.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: En inglés la frase necesita sujeto (It is clear that…); en español se puede omitir.

situacion.contexto: Sara y Carlos comentan un cuento que han leído para el club de lectura.

dialogo.texto: The protagonist, in the first person. So the narrative viewpoint is limited to what she notices.
dialogo.traduccion: La protagonista, en primera persona. Así que el punto de vista narrativo se limita a lo que ella nota.

dialogo.texto: And the tone? It sounds detached, but I think it is bitter.
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Y el tono? Suena distante, pero creo que es amargo.

dialogo.texto: I agree. We can infer that she is reluctant to admit the betrayal, because she never says his name.
dialogo.traduccion: De acuerdo. Podemos inferir que es reacia a admitir la traición, porque nunca dice su nombre.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué pista permite inferir que ella no quiere admitir la traición?

opciones.es: Que nunca dice el nombre de él.
Que cuenta la historia en tercera persona.
Que habla con un tono alegre.

item.feedback: Carlos infiere que es reacia a admitirlo «because she never says his name»: la pista es lo que calla.

guiada.consigna: ¿Qué tono domina el fragmento sobre Mia y la carta?
guiada.texto: When the letter finally arrived, Mia left it on the kitchen table for three days. She dusted around it, watered the plants beside it and told her sister, twice, that it was probably nothing important. Then, one morning, she opened it with a pen, as if it might bite.
opciones: Gently funny, with some worry behind the jokes.
Openly angry from the very first line of the passage.
Calm and detached, like a short factual report.
guiada.feedback: El humor de «as if it might bite» da un tono ligero y divertido, con cierta tensión por debajo de la broma; no hay enojo abierto ni frialdad de informe.
guiada.pista: Fíjate en la última comparación: ¿es seria o divertida, y qué esconde?

guiada.consigna: ¿Qué se puede inferir de la actitud de Mia ante la carta?
guiada.texto: When the letter finally arrived, Mia left it on the kitchen table for three days. She dusted around it, watered the plants beside it and told her sister, twice, that it was probably nothing important. Then, one morning, she opened it with a pen, as if it might bite.
opciones: She fears what the letter says but will not admit it.
She has forgotten that the letter is still on the table.
She already knows what it says and feels quite relieved about it.
guiada.feedback: Limpiar alrededor de la carta y repetir que no es importante delata miedo, aunque Mia no lo reconozca.
guiada.pista: Piensa en lo que hace durante tres días, no en lo que dice.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Mia es reacia a abrir la carta, aunque no lo admite.»
guiada.texto: Mia keeps telling her sister that the letter is probably nothing. In truth, she is ___ to open it, although she will not admit it.
guiada.feedback: Reluctant describe a quien no quiere hacer algo aunque sepa que debe hacerlo.
guiada.pista: Adjetivo que significa «reacio» y va seguido de to.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige el punto de vista y lo que revela el narrador.
practica.audio: I have never told my brother that I read his letters home from abroad. He believed the envelopes had never been opened, and for forty years I let him believe it. Was it curiosity that made me do it, or was it the fear that he would write something about me? I still cannot say. What I can say is that his handwriting changed after the second year, and that I understood why before he did.
opciones: First person: the narrator tells a secret of his own.
First person: the narrator reports what his brother later told him.
First person: the narrator admits that he misjudged his brother.
practica.feedback: El narrador dice «I have never told my brother» y cuenta su propio secreto en primera persona; no cita ninguna confesión del hermano ni reconoce haberse equivocado.

practica.consigna: ¿Qué puede inferirse del último comentario del narrador sobre la letra?
practica.texto: I have never told my brother that I read his letters home from abroad. He believed the envelopes had never been opened, and for forty years I let him believe it. Was it curiosity that made me do it, or was it the fear that he would write something about me? I still cannot say. What I can say is that his handwriting changed after the second year, and that I understood why before he did.
opciones: He understood what was happening to his brother before the brother did.
He suspected that his brother had noticed the opened envelopes.
He blames himself for having sent his brother abroad.
practica.feedback: Si entendió el cambio de letra antes que su hermano, captó lo que le ocurría antes que él: es una inferencia, no algo que el texto afirme.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada frase con el tono que transmite.
pares: «Oh, wonderful,» she said, looking at the flood in her kitchen.
He filed the report, closed the drawer and never mentioned her name again.
Every word of the toast was kind, and every word hurt a little.
She laughed at the joke, then went to wash her hands for ten minutes.
practica.feedback: El tono se deduce de la actitud que dejan ver los detalles: ironía, frialdad, amargura o nerviosismo.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige qué sugiere el final del fragmento.
evaluacion.audio: My sister called to tell me, in a bright voice, that she had finally sold our mother's piano. It was, she said, the sensible thing to do, since nobody played it any more. I told her I was very happy for her. She sounded pleased with herself, the way people do when a long argument is over. Then I put down the phone, went into the hall and looked for a long time at the empty space where the piano had been. Behind it, twenty years ago, I had hidden my first real diary. Sensible, I said aloud, to nobody. Very sensible.
opciones: Her polite approval covers resentment and a private loss.
She is relieved, since the piano had become a burden for her too.
She is proud of having kept the diary hidden for twenty years.
evaluacion.feedback: Dice que está encantada, pero repite «sensible» a solas: la ironía deja ver resentimiento y la pérdida de su escondite.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué tema sugiere el fragmento de la venta del piano?
evaluacion.texto: My sister called to tell me, in a bright voice, that she had finally sold our mother's piano. It was, she said, the sensible thing to do, since nobody played it any more. I told her I was very happy for her. She sounded pleased with herself, the way people do when a long argument is over. Then I put down the phone, went into the hall and looked for a long time at the empty space where the piano had been. Behind it, twenty years ago, I had hidden my first real diary. Sensible, I said aloud, to nobody. Very sensible.
opciones: Practical choices can take away the place where a memory lives.
Sisters who argue over their mother's things rarely forgive each other.
Sentimental objects lose their value once nobody uses them.
evaluacion.feedback: La decisión «sensata» de la hermana borra el lugar donde la narradora guardaba su diario: el tema es el coste íntimo de lo práctico, no el reparto de bienes ni el valor de los objetos.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «El informe cuenta el cierre en un tono distante, sin simpatía ni enojo.»
evaluacion.texto: The report describes the closure of the shop in a flat, ___ tone, as if nobody had lost a job. There is no kindness in it, and no anger either.
evaluacion.feedback: Un informe que cuenta una pérdida sin calidez ni enojo adopta un tono distante (detached).

evaluacion.consigna: Escribe una inferencia sobre el narrador con «We can infer that…, because…».
evaluacion.texto: I sold the house in June, and I told everybody that it was the right moment. My daughter said nothing. She simply went upstairs and took the clock from the hall, the one that had never kept the time. I pretended not to notice, and I went on talking about the price.
evaluacion.respuesta: We can infer that the narrator feels guilty, because he pretends not to notice his daughter and keeps talking about the price.
aceptadas: It is clear that he is uneasy about the sale, because he avoids looking at his daughter and goes on talking about money.
We can infer that the narrator is defensive, because he pretends not to notice the clock his daughter takes.
evaluacion.feedback: Una buena inferencia empieza con una fórmula de deducción y se apoya en una pista del texto, como fingir que no ve el reloj.

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué deja entrever el fragmento sobre la actitud del director hacia Elena?
repaso.texto: The firm's new director promised a fresh start. In his first speech he thanked everybody by name, even the newest workers, except Elena, who had trained half the team. When somebody asked about her, he smiled, did not apologise, and said that everyone had played their part. Elena smiled with the others, then quietly collected her coat.
opciones: He is downplaying her work on purpose.
He simply forgot the name of one worker.
He plans to praise her in a later speech.
repaso.feedback: Nombra hasta a los trabajadores más nuevos, omite solo a Elena, sonríe sin disculparse y responde con una generalidad: no es un olvido, minimiza su aportación a propósito.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Podemos deducir que ella es reacia a admitir la verdad.»
repaso.respuesta: We can infer that she is reluctant to admit the truth
repaso.feedback: We can infer that + oración resume una deducción; reluctant to admit + algo expresa la reticencia.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Visto ahora, lo que parecía generosidad era una traición de la confianza.»
repaso.texto: In hindsight, what looked like generosity was really a ___ of trust. He had planned it from the very first day.
repaso.feedback: Betrayal of trust es la colocación natural para romper la confianza de alguien.

classes.objetivo: Reseñar una película con descripción, dos deducciones sobre personajes, valoración con ejemplos, un defecto y una recomendación razonada.

vocabulario.es: no estar a la altura de
llevarse el protagonismo, robar la función

ensenanza.en: A gripping film holds your attention from the first scene, even when its uneven pacing makes the middle hour feel slow.
ensenanza.es: Una película absorbente capta tu atención desde la primera escena, incluso cuando su ritmo irregular hace que la hora central se sienta lenta.
ensenanza.nota: Gripping describe lo que engancha; uneven pacing, un ritmo con altibajos.

ensenanza.en: The ending feels rushed: the editor can't have had enough time to finish the last scenes of a visually stunning film.
ensenanza.es: El final parece apresurado: el editor no puede haber tenido tiempo suficiente para terminar las últimas escenas de una película visualmente deslumbrante.
ensenanza.nota: Can't have + participio deduce algo pasado; rushed describe lo hecho con prisa.

ensenanza.en: In an ensemble cast, a towering performance can steal the show, but it may also expose a flaw in the script.
ensenanza.es: En un reparto coral, una interpretación sobresaliente puede llevarse la película, pero también puede dejar al descubierto un defecto del guion.
ensenanza.nota: Steal the show: destacar tanto que eclipsa al resto; flaw es un defecto concreto.

ensenanza.en: The main character must have suspected the truth, because he avoids his brother in every scene, which makes the drama convincing.
ensenanza.es: El protagonista tuvo que sospechar la verdad, porque evita a su hermano en cada escena, y eso hace creíble el drama.
ensenanza.nota: Must have + participio: deducción casi segura apoyada en una pista; convincing = creíble.

ensenanza.en: Being utterly predictable is the film's only real flaw, and it is why the ending may fall short of the first hour.
ensenanza.es: Ser totalmente previsible es el único defecto real de la película, y por eso el final quizá no esté a la altura de la primera hora.
ensenanza.nota: Fall short of + algo: quedarse por debajo de lo esperado.

ensenanza.en: A fair review names one flaw but still decides: I would recommend it to anyone who enjoys a slow, thoughtful story.
ensenanza.es: Una reseña justa señala un defecto pero decide igualmente: yo la recomendaría a cualquiera que disfrute de una historia lenta y reflexiva.
ensenanza.nota: Recommend it to + persona, o recommend + -ing o that you + verbo; no se usa recommend + to + verbo.

explicacion.texto: Una buena reseña tiene cinco pasos: describe la película en una frase, añade dos deducciones sobre los personajes (He must have known…, She can't have meant…), valora con un ejemplo concreto (for example, in the kitchen scene…), nombra un defecto (the pacing is uneven; the ending falls short) y termina con una recomendación razonada (I would recommend it to anyone who…). Con recommend usa it to + persona, recommend + -ing o that you + verbo; no se dice «recommend to watch».

formula.texto: The film follows a woman who returns home.
Her brother must have known more than he admits,
and the dialogue is convincing: for example, in the kitchen scene…
The ending is rushed, but I would recommend it.

filas.texto: He must have… / He can't have…
I would recommend it to anyone who…

erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Recommend no admite to + verbo: se dice recommend watching o recommend that you watch.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The brother can't have knew about the letter.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: The brother can't have known about the letter.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Tras can't have va el participio (known), no el pasado simple (knew).

situacion.contexto: Mia y Leo salen del cine y comentan la película que acaban de ver.

dialogo.texto: The cast was strong, and the young lead could steal the show.
dialogo.traduccion: El reparto era sólido, y la joven protagonista podría llevarse la película.

dialogo.texto: I agree, but the ending felt rushed. The editor can't have had much time.
dialogo.traduccion: De acuerdo, pero el final pareció apresurado. El editor no puede haber tenido mucho tiempo.

dialogo.texto: And the plot was predictable. Still, I would recommend it.
dialogo.traduccion: Y la trama era previsible. Aun así, yo la recomendaría.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué defecto señala Leo?

opciones.es: Que el reparto es demasiado grande.
Que la protagonista actúa sin convicción.

item.feedback: Leo dice que «the ending felt rushed» y deduce que el editor no tuvo tiempo.

guiada.consigna: ¿Qué frase valora con un ejemplo concreto, como pide una buena reseña?
opciones: The dialogue is convincing: in the kitchen scene, two short lines reveal a whole family history.
The dialogue is very good, and everybody will enjoy it without any doubt at all.
The dialogue is the main flaw, although the director probably did his best work.
guiada.feedback: Solo la frase de la escena de la cocina apoya su opinión con un ejemplo concreto; las otras dan una opinión sin prueba o cambian de postura.
guiada.pista: Busca la opción que cita una escena concreta.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «El protagonista tuvo que saber la verdad; nunca mira a su hermano.»
guiada.texto: In every scene, the main character avoids his brother. He ___ have known the truth, because he never once looks at him.
guiada.feedback: Una pista clara permite una deducción casi segura sobre el pasado: must have + participio.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Yo se la recomendaría a cualquiera que disfrute de un misterio lento.»
guiada.respuesta: I would recommend it to anyone who enjoys a slow mystery
guiada.feedback: Recommend it to + persona cierra la reseña con una recomendación razonada.
guiada.pista: Después de recommend va it to, y luego anyone who.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige qué defecto señala el crítico en la película.
practica.audio: The first hour is gripping: the camera stays on faces, and every silence seems to hide something. But the last twenty minutes are a different film. The mystery is solved in one sentence, and the final twist feels rushed, as if the director had run out of money.
opciones: The strong opening is followed by a hurried ending.
The final twist is ruined because the film ran out of money.
The long opening hour is slowed down by too many silences.
practica.feedback: Elogia la primera hora y critica que el final se resuelva de golpe: el defecto es el ritmo apresurado; «ran out of money» es solo una comparación.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada frase de una reseña con la función que cumple.
pares: The film follows a woman who returns to her village.
Her brother must have known more than he admits.
The pacing is uneven, and the ending feels rushed.
I would recommend it to anyone who likes quiet mysteries.
practica.feedback: Cada frase cumple un paso distinto de la reseña: describir, deducir, señalar un defecto y recomendar.

practica.consigna: Completa: «La joven protagonista casi se lleva la película.»
practica.texto: The cast is excellent, but the young lead is so good that she almost ___ the show in every scene she appears in.
practica.feedback: Steal the show describe a quien destaca tanto que eclipsa al resto del reparto.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige cuál es la valoración global de la crítica.
evaluacion.audio: I went in expecting very little, and I came out a little embarrassed by how much I had enjoyed it. The script is predictable, the music is far too loud and the young lead is given lines that no one could say with a straight face. And yet I could not look away. There is a scene in a kitchen, near the end, that I am still thinking about a week later. I would not call it a great film. I would, however, recommend it to anyone who has a free evening and an open mind.
opciones: She recommends it despite clear weaknesses.
She thinks it is a great film, flaws included, and recommends it.
She enjoyed it more than she expected but hesitates to recommend it.
evaluacion.feedback: Admite defectos y dice que no es una gran película, pero la atrapó y acaba recomendándola con reservas.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Se queda corta respecto a lo que prometían sus primeros diez minutos.»
evaluacion.texto: The film is stunning to look at, but the story ___ short of the promise made by its first ten minutes.
evaluacion.feedback: Fall short of describe algo que queda por debajo de lo que prometía.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Qué deducción apoya mejor la escena descrita?
evaluacion.texto: The mother insists that she has never been to the city. In one scene, however, she gives a waiter directions to a restaurant two streets away, and her hands know exactly where the cups are kept.
opciones: She can't have been a stranger to the city.
She must have lived there for her whole life.
She might have visited once, but she has forgotten most of it.
evaluacion.feedback: Dar indicaciones y moverse con soltura contradice que sea una desconocida; decir que vivió allí toda la vida sería ir demasiado lejos, y olvidar una visita no explica su soltura.

evaluacion.consigna: Escribe una reseña con dos deducciones, un ejemplo, un defecto y una recomendación.
evaluacion.texto: Película ficticia «El puerto callado»: una mujer vuelve a su aldea pesquera tras diez años. Su hermano no la mira durante la boda, y la vecina, que jura que no salió de casa esa noche, tiene las botas llenas de barro. En una escena de la cocina, dos frases bastan para revelar toda la historia familiar. El reparto es excelente y los diálogos son creíbles, pero el final es apresurado. Escribe una reseña de al menos 120 palabras (lo ideal, 200).
evaluacion.respuesta: The Quiet Harbour follows a woman who returns to her fishing village after ten years and finds that nobody wants to talk about the night her father disappeared. From the first scene, the film is gripping: the camera stays on faces, and every silence seems to hide something. The cast is excellent, and the young lead almost steals the show. Her brother must have known more than he admits, because he never looks at her during the wedding, and the old neighbour, who says she never left her house, can't have stayed in that night, since her boots were covered in mud. The dialogue is convincing, for example in the kitchen scene, where two sentences reveal a whole family history. The one flaw is the pacing: the final twist feels rushed, and the ending may fall short of the promise of the first hour. Even so, I would highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys a slow, thoughtful mystery.
aceptadas: The Quiet Harbour is about a woman who goes back to her village by the sea after ten years. The film is stunning to look at and the actors are very good. Her brother must have hidden something from her, because he avoids her eyes at the wedding. The neighbour can't have stayed at home that night, since her boots were full of mud. The dialogue feels real, for instance in the kitchen scene, where a few words explain the whole family. The main weakness is that the story is predictable and the ending is rushed, so it falls short of its beginning. Nevertheless, I recommend it to everybody who likes slow films with a mystery, because the performances alone are worth the ticket.
evaluacion.feedback: Una reseña completa describe la película, deduce con modales perfectos, valora con un ejemplo, nombra un defecto y recomienda con una razón.

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué da a entender la crítica sobre la película con sus elogios?
repaso.texto: The film is well made. The actors arrive on time, the camera is usually in focus, and the ending comes, as promised, at ninety minutes. One could hardly ask for more, and one does not get it. I left the cinema in a good mood, which had gone before I reached the bus stop.
opciones: She finds it acceptable but soon forgotten.
She dislikes it because it runs longer than promised.
She is impressed by its skill and its care.
repaso.feedback: Alaba solo lo básico (llegar a tiempo, enfocar) y señala que la sensación se esfumó: es un elogio frío que sugiere una película olvidable, no admiración ni queja por la duración.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «El ritmo es irregular y el giro final parece apresurado.»
repaso.respuesta: The pacing is uneven and the final twist feels rushed
repaso.feedback: Dos defectos unidos con and: el ritmo irregular y el giro final apresurado.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «El reparto es magnífico: hasta los papeles pequeños están cuidados.»
repaso.texto: Even the smallest roles are played with care. The ___ is excellent, and every scene feels lived in.
repaso.feedback: El reparto (cast) es el conjunto de actores de una película.

classes.objetivo: Debatir una historia en un club de lectura: proponer una lectura, defenderla con dos deducciones, conceder un punto y discrepar con educación.

ensenanza.en: I would argue that the ending is ambiguous on purpose, since the writer never says which version is true.
ensenanza.es: Yo sostendría que el final es ambiguo a propósito, ya que la autora nunca dice qué versión es la verdadera.
ensenanza.nota: I would argue that… propone una lectura con prudencia; ambiguous admite más de una interpretación.

ensenanza.en: Some readers interpret the closed door as regret, yet a plausible reading is that she must have felt relieved.
ensenanza.es: Algunos lectores interpretan la puerta cerrada como arrepentimiento, pero una lectura verosímil es que ella tuvo que sentirse aliviada.
ensenanza.nota: Plausible reading: una interpretación creíble según las pruebas; must have + participio deduce.

ensenanza.en: You can argue your view more strongly if you make a case for it with two clues from the text, not with feelings.
ensenanza.es: Puedes defender tu postura con más fuerza si la argumentas con dos pistas del texto, y no con sentimientos.
ensenanza.nota: Make a case for + algo: defenderlo con pruebas ordenadas.

ensenanza.en: I take issue with that view; I am not convinced that the argument will hold water once we reread the last page.
ensenanza.es: Discrepo de ese punto de vista; no estoy convencido de que el argumento se sostenga cuando releamos la última página.
ensenanza.nota: Take issue with es discrepar con firmeza; hold water, resistir una comprobación.

ensenanza.en: A fair debater will concede that a clue is strong and will not read too much into a single detail.
ensenanza.es: Quien debate con justicia admitirá que una pista es sólida y no le dará demasiada interpretación a un solo detalle.
ensenanza.nota: Concede that… admite un punto sin cambiar de postura; read too much into, sobreinterpretar.

ensenanza.en: When two readers still argue after an hour, agree to disagree, or play devil's advocate to test your own view.
ensenanza.es: Cuando dos lectores todavía discuten después de una hora, conviene aceptar que se piensa distinto o hacer de abogado del diablo para poner a prueba la propia opinión.
ensenanza.nota: Agree to disagree cierra un debate con respeto; play devil's advocate, defender lo contrario por método.

explicacion.titulo: Defender una lectura sin cerrar el debate
explicacion.texto: En un club de lectura no hay una única respuesta correcta. Propón tu lectura con prudencia (I would argue that…, A plausible reading is…), defiéndela con dos deducciones apoyadas en pistas (must have, can't have, might have) y reconoce lo que el otro acierte (I concede that…, You make a fair point). Si no te convence, discrepa con tacto: I take issue with…, I am not entirely convinced. Cierra con respeto: We will have to agree to disagree. Este debate reúne todo el bloque: pistas del narrador, vocabulario literario y valoración con pruebas.

formula.texto: I would argue that the ending is ambiguous,
because the narrator can't have been honest.
formula.nota: primera deducción apoyada en una pista

formula.texto: I concede that your reading is plausible,
formula.nota: reconoces lo válido de la otra lectura

formula.texto: but I am not convinced.

filas.texto: I would argue that it is ambiguous.
I concede that… / You make a fair point
I concede that it is plausible.
I take issue with… / I am not convinced
I am not convinced by that reading.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I am not agree with your reading.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: I do not agree with your reading.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Agree es un verbo, no un adjetivo: se niega con do not agree, no con am not agree.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The narrator must to have lied.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Los modales no llevan to: must have + participio.

situacion.contexto: En el club de lectura, Sara y Carlos discuten el final de una novela.

dialogo.texto: I would argue that the ending is ambiguous on purpose.
dialogo.traduccion: Yo sostendría que el final es ambiguo a propósito.

dialogo.texto: I am not convinced. The narrator can't have been honest, so the ending is a lie.
dialogo.traduccion: No me convence. El narrador no puede haber sido sincero, así que el final es una mentira.

dialogo.texto: That is a plausible reading, and I concede it. But I take issue with your last step.
dialogo.traduccion: Es una lectura verosímil, y lo admito. Pero discrepo de tu último paso.

dialogo.texto: Fair enough. Shall we agree to disagree?

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿con qué discrepa Sara al final?

opciones.es: Con la conclusión de que el final es una mentira.
Con la idea de que el narrador fuera sincero.
Con la propuesta de releer la novela.

item.feedback: Sara admite que la lectura de Carlos es verosímil, pero discrepa de su último paso: pasar de la falta de sinceridad a un final que es una mentira.

guiada.consigna: ¿Qué respuesta admite un punto sin abandonar la propia lectura?
opciones: I see your point, and I concede it, but I read the ending differently.
I concede everything you say, so I must have been wrong from the start.
That point is fair, which is exactly why your reading cannot be plausible.
guiada.feedback: Concede un punto concreto y mantiene su lectura con but; la que lo concede todo renuncia a su lectura y la que niega lo que admite se contradice.
guiada.pista: Busca la opción que reconoce el punto y, aun así, mantiene la propia lectura.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Yo sostendría que ambas lecturas son verosímiles.»
guiada.texto: Some readers say the narrator lied. Others say he was only afraid. I would ___ that both readings are plausible.
guiada.feedback: I would argue that… es la fórmula prudente para proponer una lectura.
guiada.pista: Verbo que significa «sostener» y va seguido de that.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Tendremos que aceptar que pensamos distinto sobre la última página.»
guiada.respuesta: We will have to agree to disagree about the last page
guiada.feedback: Agree to disagree cierra el debate con respeto, sin que nadie tenga que ceder.
guiada.pista: Empieza con We will have to y termina con about the last page.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige en qué discrepa la hablante.
practica.audio: I take issue with that reading. You say the narrator lied because he was nervous, but nervous people are not always liars. To my mind, the letter is the real clue. If she knew the truth, she must have hidden it, and he might have found it much later.
opciones: She thinks being nervous is not solid proof that he lied.
She agrees that he lied, but thinks the letter explains why.
She finds the letter a weaker clue than his being nervous.
practica.feedback: Discrepa de que el nerviosismo sea prueba de mentira y propone la carta como pista más fiable; no acepta que mintiera.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada fórmula del club de lectura con su función.
practica.feedback: Cada fórmula cumple un paso distinto del debate: proponer, discrepar, conceder y cerrar.

practica.consigna: Completa: «Ese argumento no se sostiene cuando relees el primer capítulo.»
practica.texto: You say the narrator is lying because he is nervous. But that argument does not hold ___ once you reread the first chapter.
practica.feedback: Hold water se usa para un argumento que resiste una comprobación.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige qué actitud muestra Carlos al final de la discusión.
evaluacion.audio: At the club, Carlos argued for an hour that the narrator was a liar. Sara listened, nodded at the right moments, and then said that he made a fair point about the letter, and that she would gladly concede it. What she could not accept, she said, was that one lie makes every page a lie. A reader who reads too much into one detail ends up writing a different novel. Carlos smiled, looked at the ceiling and suggested that they should agree to disagree, which, everyone understood, meant that he had not changed his mind either.
opciones: He keeps his view but ends the debate politely.
He concedes Sara's point and quietly drops his accusation.
He hopes the suggestion will persuade Sara to change her mind.
evaluacion.feedback: Proponer aceptar el desacuerdo, sonriendo, y el narrador aclara que tampoco cambió de opinión: mantiene su postura y cierra con educación.

evaluacion.consigna: ¿Para qué dice la autora que hará de abogada del diablo?
evaluacion.texto: Dear all, before Thursday, could you each send one piece of evidence for your reading of the ending? I will play devil's advocate at the meeting: whatever you argue, I will take issue with it, so please choose clues that can hold water. I am not entirely convinced by any version so far, including my own.
opciones: To test how well each reading is supported.
To push members to adopt her own reading of the ending.
To show that the ending has no plausible reading.
evaluacion.feedback: Dice que discrepará de cualquier postura para que cada miembro elija pistas sólidas; ella misma duda de su propia versión, así que no busca imponer la suya.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Debo admitir que la última línea lo apoya, pero el resto del libro no.»
evaluacion.texto: Tom says the ending is a happy one. I must ___ that the last line supports him, but the rest of the book does not.
evaluacion.feedback: Concede that… admite un punto del otro sin renunciar a la propia lectura.

evaluacion.consigna: Escribe tu intervención: lectura, dos deducciones, concesión y cierre respetuoso.
evaluacion.texto: Club de lectura. La novela «The Blue Door» termina así: el narrador cierra la puerta azul de la casa y dice «Nobody ever lived here». Antes contó que su hermana se fue tras una discusión y que la carta de ella apareció mojada. Carlos cree que el narrador miente. Escribe tu intervención (al menos 135 palabras; ideal, 220): propón tu lectura, defiéndela con dos deducciones, concede un punto, discrepa con tacto y cierra con respeto.
evaluacion.respuesta: I would argue that the ending of The Blue Door is ambiguous on purpose. The narrator says that nobody ever lived in the house, but he can't have been honest, because he also says that his sister left after an argument. The wet letter is a clue: she must have been upset when she wrote it, and he might have kept it hidden for years. A plausible reading is that the blue door is a symbol of a memory that he cannot close. Carlos argues that the narrator is simply lying to us, and I concede that this is possible. However, I take issue with the idea that one lie spoils the whole book, and I am not entirely convinced that the writer wants us to be certain. But we should not read too much into one lie. The imagery of cold and rain makes the sadness resonate, and the ending stays open to interpretation. We will have to agree to disagree, Carlos.
aceptadas: In my reading, the last scene is ambiguous, and the blue door is a symbol of memory. The narrator can't have been telling the whole truth, because the letter was wet, so somebody must have read it or hidden it. His sister might have left in anger, and he might have closed the door to forget her. Carlos says that the narrator is lying, and I concede that this is plausible, because the clues contradict him. Even so, I am not convinced that the writer wants a clear answer, and I think it is wrong to read too much into one detail. The cold imagery conveys sadness, and the ending will resonate with anyone who has lost someone. You make a fair point, Carlos, but we will have to agree to disagree.
evaluacion.feedback: Una buena intervención propone una lectura, la apoya con dos deducciones, admite el punto del otro, discrepa con tacto y cierra con respeto.

repaso.consigna: ¿Qué actitud muestra la autora de este mensaje tras el debate?
repaso.texto: Thank you all for a lively evening. I must have sounded stubborn, and I might have been; in fact, I went home and read the last chapter again, and I can't say that I am still certain. I am not ready to change my reading, but I am ready to admit that the matter is less simple than I claimed.
opciones: She keeps her view but admits some doubt.
She now doubts every reading, including the other members'.
She is annoyed that nobody agreed with her.
repaso.feedback: No cambia su lectura, pero reconoce que el asunto es menos simple de lo que sostenía: mantiene su postura con una duda.

repaso.consigna: Ordena: «Es fácil darle demasiada interpretación a un solo detalle.»
repaso.respuesta: It is easy to read too much into a single detail
repaso.feedback: Read too much into + algo describe sobreinterpretar un detalle aislado.

repaso.consigna: Concede un punto, pero mantén tu lectura.
repaso.texto: Un compañero dice que el narrador miente. Tú admites que es verosímil, pero sigues pensando que el final es ambiguo.
repaso.respuesta: I concede that your reading is plausible, but I still find the ending ambiguous.
aceptadas: I admit that it is possible, but I would argue that the ending is open to interpretation.
repaso.feedback: Se concede el punto con I concede that y se mantiene la lectura con but.
